historicalContext.zh: 拉脫維亞語與立陶宛語同屬波羅的語族，是現存僅有的兩種波羅的語言，與愛沙尼亞語（屬烏拉爾語系）明顯不同；境內俄語人口比例高（約三分之一在家中使用俄語），東部拉特加萊地區則有拉特加萊語（拉脫維亞語的一種變體，具原住民語言地位）偶爾出現在地方路牌上。1992年拉脫維亞加入維也納道路標誌公約，獨立後另訂新標誌系統，取代蘇聯時期沿用的舊制。
historicalContext.en: Latvian and Lithuanian are the only two surviving Baltic languages, clearly distinct from Estonian (which belongs to the Uralic family). A large Russian-speaking minority remains (roughly a third of the population speaks Russian at home), and Latgalian — a Latvian variety with indigenous-language recognition in eastern Latgale — occasionally appears on local signage. Latvia acceded to the Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals in 1992 and developed a new post-independence sign standard, replacing the Soviet-era system still used elsewhere.
